title: Subdural Empyema, Epidural Abscess, and Suppurative Thrombophlebitis

parts.text: Cavernous sinus thrombosis - 4 cranial nerves involved and an associated sign/symptom with each nerve

questions.model_answer: 4 cranial nerves traversing the cavernous sinus and associated findings: (1) CN III (oculomotor) - ptosis, mydriasis (dilated pupil), and the eye deviated "down and out"; (2) CN IV (trochlear) - impaired downward/inward eye movement causing vertical diplopia worse on looking down; (3) CN V (trigeminal, V1 ophthalmic and V2 maxillary divisions) - facial pain/numbness/paresthesia over the forehead, periorbital region, and cheek; (4) CN VI (abducens) - lateral rectus palsy causing inability to abduct the eye and horizontal diplopia (often the earliest/most sensitive sign, as CN VI runs freely within the sinus rather than in its lateral wall).

questions.question: Patient upper resp infection/sinus. A few weeks later, headache, low grade fever.

parts.text: What is the name of the syndrome and complication (as seen on the image provided - picture of forehead abscess and a subdural abscess - Pott's puffy tumor)
What is the organism or group of organisms that is the most likely pathogen

questions.model_answer:
a) Syndrome/complication: Pott's puffy tumor (frontal bone osteomyelitis with subperiosteal frontal abscess) complicated by an associated subdural empyema, arising from frontal sinusitis.
b) Most likely pathogen/group: Streptococcus anginosus (milleri) group.
c) 4 other common organisms: Staphylococcus aureus, Haemophilus influenzae, anaerobes (Fusobacterium and Prevotella spp.), and Enterobacteriaceae (e.g., Klebsiella, E. coli).
d) Empiric treatment: vancomycin + a third-generation cephalosporin (ceftriaxone or cefotaxime) + metronidazole.

questions.question:
Q32 (2017)
5 year old child has orbital cellulitis complicated by cavernous sinus thrombosis.

parts.text: A) List 3 findings that suggest orbital vs pre-orbital cellulitis?
B) Fill this table regarding which cranial nerves are affected by cavernous sinus thrombosis and 4 common symptoms and signs: CN III (oculomotor), IV (trochlear), V (trigeminal), VI (abducens)

cohort_answer.text:
A) Proptosis, Pain on extraocular movements, Ophthalmoplegia, Diplopia, Chemosis.

B) III (oculomotor): Downward (SO4), outward gaze (LR6), dilated pupil. IV (trochlear): Hypertropia, head tilt. V (trigeminal): Deviation of the jaw, paresthesias, pain, inability to chew or bite down. VI (abducens): esotropia.
